comment: positive: a variable named like an unreserved keyword is a valid assignment target
body: DECLARE forward int := 21; BEGIN forward := forward * 2; END

comment: positive: a bound cursor FOR loop is accepted (reads as a query FOR)
body: DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 1; BEGIN FOR r IN c LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: negative: assignment to a CONSTANT variable is rejected
body: DECLARE x CONSTANT int := 1; BEGIN x := 2; END

comment: negative: assignment to a field of a CONSTANT is rejected via the parent
body: DECLARE x CONSTANT int[] := '{1}'; BEGIN x[1] := 2; END

comment: negative: CONTINUE outside a loop is rejected
body: BEGIN CONTINUE; END
error: CONTINUE cannot be used outside a loop

comment: negative: unlabeled EXIT outside a loop is rejected
body: BEGIN EXIT; END
error: EXIT cannot be used outside a loop, unless it has a label

comment: negative: EXIT referencing a nonexistent label is rejected
body: BEGIN LOOP EXIT no_such_label; END LOOP; END

comment: negative: CONTINUE targeting a block label is rejected
body: BEGIN <<blk>> BEGIN LOOP CONTINUE blk; END LOOP; END; END
error: block label "blk" cannot be used in CONTINUE

comment: negative: a cursor FOR loop over an unbound cursor is rejected
body: DECLARE c refcursor; BEGIN FOR r IN c LOOP END LOOP; END
error: cursor FOR loop must use a bound cursor variable

comment: positive: a RECORD variable field is a resolved assignment target
body: DECLARE r RECORD; BEGIN r.f := 1; END

comment: positive: %ROWTYPE is recognized as a record
body: DECLARE r sometable%ROWTYPE; BEGIN r.a := 1; END

comment: negative: assignment to a field of a CONSTANT record is rejected
body: DECLARE r CONSTANT RECORD; BEGIN r.f := 1; END

comment: negative: a CONSTANT comma-listed FOR target is rejected
body: DECLARE x CONSTANT int := 1; y int; BEGIN FOR x, y IN SELECT 1, 2 LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: negative: an undeclared query-FOR loop target is rejected
body: BEGIN FOR r IN SELECT 1 LOOP END LOOP; END
error: loop variable of loop over rows must be a record variable or list of scalar variables

comment: negative: an undeclared FOREACH loop target is rejected
body: BEGIN FOREACH x IN ARRAY a LOOP END LOOP; END
error: loop variable of FOREACH must be a known variable or list of variables

comment: positive: a bound cursor FOR loop supplies its own record variable (undeclared target is fine)
body: DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 1; BEGIN FOR r IN c LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: an integer FOR loop variable resolves in the body, so `i = i + 1` is an assignment (deparses :=), not a SQL statement
body: BEGIN FOR i IN 1..10 LOOP i = i + 1; END LOOP; END

comment: a bound cursor FOR builds a record loop variable, so `r.x = 1` in the body resolves to a field assignment
body: DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 1; BEGIN FOR r IN c LOOP r.x = 1; END LOOP; END

comment: a CONSTANT record member in a comma-list FOR target reports CONSTANT first (check_assignable before the not-a-scalar test)
body: DECLARE r CONSTANT RECORD; s int; BEGIN FOR s, r IN SELECT 1, 2 LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: an ALIAS reuses the target's datum, so assigning through an alias of a CONSTANT is rejected (names the target)
body: DECLARE x CONSTANT int := 1; y ALIAS FOR x; BEGIN y := 2; END

comment: an ALIAS of a record resolves alias.field
body: DECLARE r RECORD; a ALIAS FOR r; BEGIN a.f := 1; END

comment: a GET DIAGNOSTICS target that is a record is rejected as not a scalar variable
body: DECLARE r RECORD; BEGIN GET DIAGNOSTICS r := ROW_COUNT; END

comment: a variable named like a diagnostics keyword does not shadow the keyword in the GET DIAGNOSTICS item position (PG's tok_is_keyword)
body: DECLARE row_count int; n int; BEGIN GET DIAGNOSTICS n := ROW_COUNT; END

comment: a variable named like a RAISE option does not shadow the option keyword (PG's tok_is_keyword)
body: DECLARE message text; BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION USING MESSAGE = 'x'; END

comment: sqlerrm is an implicit CONSTANT in a handler, so assigning to it is rejected
body: BEGIN NULL; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN sqlerrm := 'x'; END

comment: sqlstate is an implicit CONSTANT in a handler, so assigning to it is rejected
body: BEGIN NULL; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN sqlstate := '00000'; END

comment: a variable named like a RAISE level does not shadow the level keyword (tok_is_keyword)
body: DECLARE notice int; BEGIN RAISE notice 'hello'; END

comment: a variable named like RETURN QUERY does not shadow the QUERY keyword (tok_is_keyword)
body: DECLARE query int; BEGIN RETURN QUERY SELECT 1; END

comment: a variable named like a FETCH direction does not shadow the direction keyword (tok_is_keyword)
body: DECLARE backward int; c refcursor; x int; BEGIN FETCH backward FROM c INTO x; END

comment: a variable named like REVERSE does not shadow the integer-FOR keyword (tok_is_keyword)
body: DECLARE reverse int; BEGIN FOR i IN reverse 10..1 LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: a lone compound query-FOR target is accepted (no catalog: r.x could be a field of a named-composite record PG resolves; superset, not fail-closed)
body: DECLARE r somecomposite; BEGIN FOR r.x IN SELECT 1 LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: a lone compound FOREACH target is accepted for the same no-catalog reason
body: DECLARE r somecomposite; BEGIN FOREACH r.x IN ARRAY a LOOP END LOOP; END

comment: a lone PLAIN undeclared query-FOR target is still rejected (it cannot be a field, matching PG)
body: BEGIN FOR nope IN SELECT 1 LOOP END LOOP; END
error: loop variable of loop over rows must be a record variable or list of scalar variables
